Sentence (English): This DW seems to get good reviews, and after using it for awhile, I am perplexed.
Comments (English): [ Not the best dishwasher, that's for sure ] || ---------------- || This DW seems to get good reviews, and after using it for awhile, I am perplexed. No, it's not a bad DW, but geez, just some little things that drive me crazy. The little prongs that go up or down depending on pots in the lower rack? They seem to like to be down - really cheap and they consistently fall over, meaning plates won't stay upright. I ended up wiring the prongs to keep them up. The upper rack seems to be very loose and flimsy, hard to push in. We figured out how to get dishes dry by online searches, so we got that fixed - although having to have the door ajar after ever wash cycle is a pain. You can disable it, but then the dishes don't completely dry. The silverware holder on the right is not secure and slides around. All in all this is just a cheap dishwasher with a not so cheap price. Not a fan.

Sentence (English): It's hard to write a review for a product like this.
Comments (English): [ Washes dishes fine but could have caused a fire ] || ---------------- || It's hard to write a review for a product like this. The dishwasher worked just fine for two years and one month, and then conked out because the Bosch-supplied electrical junction box had essentially burned up. The electrical cable on the outside of the box was singed, and the interior of the box was a charred mess. I cannot say whether the problem was due to a design problem with the box, a faulty installation (it was installed by an authorized Bosch dealer), or some combination of the above (a design that makes it difficult to install properly). I do see that there are other people who've experienced this problem with Bosch junction boxes. We had no indication that there was anything amiss until the dishwasher wouldn't turn on. No burning smell, and no visual indication since the box is hidden under the cabinets. A junction box performs one simple function, so this was quite a surprise. Our previous dishwasher of a different brand was also hardwired like this, and was still working after 23 years when we decided to replace it with a quieter model. We're uncomfortable simply replacing the junction box with a new one because we'll have no way of knowing if it's experiencing the same problem, and from searches we can see that some other people have had this problem, too. Instead, we're going to install an electrical outlet so that we can dispense with the junction box. The unit is beyond its one-year parts and labor warranty, but still warrantied for electrical components. Bosch was kind enough to reimburse us for the labor cost of diagnosing this safety issue. Even so, we're still on the hook for what I anticipate being upwards of $400 to have an electrician install a power outlet, and the labor for the appliance dealer to replace the control board (which they're doing in case power line instability or arcing damaged it) and then reinstall the dishwasher. That's getting close to 50% of the original cost of the dishwasher. So how do you average things out when rating a product that usually performs well, but which seemingly, for whatever reason, could have burned down your house? Although the dishwasher worked quite well, we now regret buying it, considering the extra cost, extended inconvenience, and the safety issue.

Sentence (English): It's only been two days, but I've developed a dishwashing routine.
Comments (English): [ The world is so convenient. ] || ---------------- || It's only been two days, but I've developed a dishwashing routine. I make a cup of coffee, place it on the table, and then go to the sink and run the dishwasher. (If you use a Java faucet, it might be easier to use it with a drip tray.) It takes more than a minute to drain, so you can do some preliminary washing up in that time. I stack the dishes in a Tetris-like pattern, add detergent, and press the start button. The instructions say to use 6 grams, but I use a 10-gram all-in-one detergent, cut in half. Technically, it's only 5 grams, but that difference doesn't matter. It washes the dishes well. Then I wash the sink strainer, wipe down the sink, and wipe down the table. By the time I'm done, the coffee is cooled to the perfect temperature. After I drink my coffee, the dishwasher starts to wash (it seems to take a while to warm up). I press the pause button, put my cup in, and I'm done for the day. Later, I just open the door, put the dishes away, and put them away. On days when there were a lot of dishes, I used to feel a little tired after washing them, but now I feel like I have more time. Buy a dishwasher. You really should.

Comments (English): [ Too loud and stays wet inside. ] || ---------------- || I purchased this dishwasher and it was delivered the very next day. I'm returning it because it is very loud, you can hear the swishing noise of the water. It also does not dry the dishes very well at all. Any cup, mug or glass that had the slightest lip on the bottom had water that I had to use a towel to dry the bottoms before putting in the cabinet. The entire inside of this dishwasher was wet after running and stayed wet. I even dried the inside of the door off several times and every time it was opened again it was wet. The entire bottom of the machine was also wet. So, leaving the door open while emptying it you would end up with water on the floor as well. I also didn't find the inside racks to be very big at all. They seemed much smaller and held less dishes than my previous dishwasher. So I would say if you're on a budget then maybe this is the one for you but for me for the money it was just not worth it.

Sentence (English): We needed to replace a dishwasher that I thought was perfect until it melted (deformed) my dishes and leaked into the basement.
Comments (English): [ Hadn't known what I was missing! ] || ---------------- || We needed to replace a dishwasher that I thought was perfect until it melted (deformed) my dishes and leaked into the basement. We replaced it with this Whirlpool, not thinking about new features, but just replacing what we had. What a pleasant surprise. The top shelf was a bonus and is so convenient for those awkward items that seem to get in the way. The second shelf is also adjustable so that all the tall items that we used to wash by hand, now fit. And the bottom shelf is just like any other dishwasher, but with more room so that the sprayers don't hit the taller items. Not only is this dishwasher a new kind of convenient, it honestly does clean the dishes better than the really nice dishwasher we had before—and it didn't melt our dishwasher safe bowls! The only negative would be that because the interior has so much more room, the bottom shelf obviously had to be a little lower than a normal capacity appliance—not enough to make a difference for most, I would think. I am sorry our old dishwasher failed so miserably but quite happy we ended up with this one. It has been a great purchase.

Comments (English): [ Cleans exceptionally well ] || ---------------- || The research & reviews influenced our purchase. This dishwasher was to replace our 20 yr old GE Profile crappy dishwasher. It was actually stressful to use our old dishwasher; having to rinse & scrub all dishes before running a load. We selected the streamlined (no handle) SS model. It is truly a modern & clean design that holds no fingerprints! The 3rd tier is a great feature. The ProWash/ProDry cycle is amazing. I just scrape of any loose foods off the dishes & load them. It usually take us 2-3 days to accumulate a full load. That means dried on, crusty, greasy dishes. But, if for some reason I need to run a small load sooner, there is cycle that runs only for the top 2 tiers of the dishwasher! It runs super quiet. And most importantly, the dishes (pots too) come out SPOTLESS and dry! A dishwasher that does the job it was designed to do. The only minor blips are the price (it is expensive) & that very few of the basket times collapse flat. We are extremely pleased with this KitchenAid dishwasher.

I hate this dishwasher with a passion and wouldn't recommend it.

Sentence (English): The height of Midea's 5 sets of dishwashers is 500 compared with similar ones, and the height of other 5-6 sets is generally 600.
Comments (English): The height of Midea's 5 sets of dishwashers is 500 compared with similar ones, and the height of other 5-6 sets is generally 600. Therefore, this relatively high plate will be somewhat limited, and the bowl rack on the upper level needs to be disassembled when necessary. But the biggest advantage of this machine is that the inner wall, including the inner side of the door, is made of aluminum alloy, and the quality is also very good. Various washing methods including separate drying and storage can be realized on the door panel. But what I complain about is that the detailed description of this machine is too simple, and the electronic instructions in the page introduction do not match. After purchasing the machine, the manual is actually not very clear. I found it in Midea. clear. In addition, this machine does not have a special place for dishwashing tablets and polishes. The dishwashing tablets can be placed directly in the machine. If you want to buy this machine, you don’t need to buy polish separately. The machine is very clean, overall very satisfied.
Comments (Original): 美的这款5套洗碗机与同类相比高度是500，其他5-6套一般是600高。所以这款放相对高一点的盘子会有些受限制，必要的时候需要拆卸上一层的碗栏。但是这款机器的最大优点是内壁包括门内侧全部是铝合金材质，质量也很棒，多种洗涤方式包括单独的烘干储存在门板上都可以实现。但是比较吐槽的是这款机器详细说明太简单，页面介绍里面的电子说明也不匹配，购机后说明书其实也不是很清楚，我是在美的家居中找到的我的机器得详细说明才最后搞明白。另外这台机器没有专门放洗碗块和亮光剂的地方，洗碗块直接放在机器里面即可，想买这台机器就不要单独买亮光剂了。机器清洗很干净，总体非常满意。

Normally the super duper stuck food would have been scraped off prior to placing in the dishwasher. Unlike our older model, I really like that pre-rinsing is almost never required and the the LED screen clearly advises time left for cycle completion. Looks very modern. Uses less than 4 gallons of water per wash! Less water than hand washing! Although still in the honeymoon stage, at this point, we are not disappointed in the least with our decision on this model.

Looking forward to our new Bosch that we know will be FAR superior to this one.

Sentence (English): I had a Fagor dishwasher from before, which has lasted me 27 years without a single repair and it washed great.
Comments (English): [ I expected something better ] || ---------------- || I had a Fagor dishwasher from before, which has lasted me 27 years without a single repair and it washed great. It was crude and without electronics (mechanical programmer, it was quite noisy, etc.), but it washed great and in 27 years not a single problem. In the end, the poor guy said enough is enough and I opted for this Bosch with some reluctance because the Wi-Fi issue seems to me nonsense that all it does is add pointless electronics and make things more expensive. It does not wash well, it leaves the crockery quite wet, and nothing that has a slightly consistent stain, the crockery comes out dirty (which did not happen with the old Fagor). Of course, it is beautiful and very quiet, but I have been disappointed. I have tried the eco program (very long) and the automatic one, and the results are similar. The issue of the app and the Wi-Fi, nonsense that I uninstalled at minute 0. Anyway, I don't recommend it, I have another from a supposedly inferior brand (Beko) in another house and it washes much better. It will be necessary to see how long it lasts, because it is already known that now they do things so that they last less than 10 years.
Comments (Original): [ Esperaba algo mejor ] || ---------------- || Tenía un lavavajillas Fagor de los de antes, que me ha durado 27 años sin una sola reparación y lavaba genial. Era tosco y sin electrónica (programador mecánico, hacía bastante ruido, etc), pero lavaba genial y en 27 años ni un solo problema. Al final el pobre dijo basta y opté por este Bosch con ciertas reticencias porque el tema del wifi me parece una majadería que lo único que hace es meter electrónica sin sentido y encarecer las cosas. No lava bien, deja la vajilla bastante mojada, y a nada que haya alguna mancha un poco consistente, sale sucia la vajilla (lo cual no ocurría con el viejo Fagor). Eso sí, es bonito y muy silencioso, pero me he llevado una decepción. He probado con el programa eco (larguísimo) y el automático, y los resultados son similares. El tema de la app y el wifi, una tontería que desinstalé al minuto 0. En fin, no lo recomiendo, tengo otro de una marca supuestamente inferior (Beko) en otra casa y lava muchísimo mejor. Habrá que ver cuánto dura, porque ya se sabe que ahora hacen las cosas para que duren menos de 10 años.

The concierge team at Costco did a great job in ordering the part for me and having them delivered, with great follow-up with me. The dishwasher is very "plasticky": light door, no glass holder for wine glasses. but it is very quiet.

Comments (English): [ My new dishwasher ] || ---------------- || All the world raved about what a great product Bosch makes. I was excited to get a Bosch dishwasher. The dish racks were disapointing. They look like they hold a lot, but the shape and size of my dishes don't seem compatible. Also, the tines are so close together, I can't understand how they can get dishes clean without double spacing them. The silverware baskets are very disapointing. My silverware has big handles that cannot fit in the guides so I removed the guides. The baskets don't hang on the rack as well as they should. The bottom rack doesn't roll across the door opening well and I find myself having to put it back on track often. The display on the front is great however the dishwasher doesn't remember the last wash setting. It defaults to auto and I don't trust the auto feature to clean my dishes so I change it every time. It's hard to understand why it takes two hours to wash and dry dishes. Seems like a long time to me. The door stays down when open but as you close it, the last little bit of travel the pulls the door closed hard. Again, maybe by design, but we like to leave our door open a bit for air circulation when the dishwasher is not in use. I wanted a 300 or 500 series dishwasher but could not find one ANYWHERE in black color. None of the big box stores, none of the local appliance stores. Not sure why, but again, disapointment as my old dishwasher could not be repaired and I needed a new one immediately. So, I had to settle. Another positive, it doesn't have WIFI.

Sentence (English): We love our Bosch 800 Series dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great Dishwasher - some minor annoyances ] || ---------------- || We love our Bosch 800 Series dishwasher. It's whisper quiet and does a fantastic job cleaning the dishes. I like the red light indicator - the dishwasher is so quiet, it's hard to tell when it's on and running. I have three annoyances with it, however. First, when the bottom rack is not fully loaded it can easily slide off the track. Second, the tines along the back of the bottom rack extend all the way to the edge, and so placing any large pan or cookie sheet is difficult. They need to end, one row in, allowing large pan placement. Finally, the silverware trays are garbage. For a premium dishwasher, Bosch should have done a better job with these. They do not stay stuck to the rack, and flop around everywhere. They are also too low, so that large kitchen spoons, spantulas, etc topple over (and then so does the basket because it isn't secured well.) Fix these things and the dishwasher will be perfect.Even with these small annoyances, we would still very much recommend the Bosch 800 series.

Oh, and no manual is given to find out all the features, so I have to hunt them down. Once I do, I might change this to 5 stars, but it's a good solid 4 for now.

Sentence (English): I had a Fagor dishwasher from before, which has lasted me 27 years without a single repair and it washed great.
Comments (English): [ I expected something better ] || ---------------- || I had a Fagor dishwasher from before, which has lasted me 27 years without a single repair and it washed great. It was crude and without electronics (mechanical programmer, it was quite noisy, etc.), but it washed great and in 27 years not a single problem. In the end, the poor guy said enough is enough and I opted for this Bosch with some reluctance because the Wi-Fi issue seems to me nonsense that all it does is insert pointless electronics and make things more expensive. It does not wash well, it leaves the crockery quite wet, and nothing that has a slightly consistent stain, the crockery comes out dirty (which did not happen with the old Fagor). Of course, it is beautiful and very quiet, but I have been disappointed. I have tried the eco program (very long) and the automatic one, and the results are similar. The issue of the app and the Wi-Fi, nonsense that I uninstalled at minute 0. Anyway, I don't recommend it, I have another from a supposedly inferior brand (Beko) in another house and it washes much better. It will be necessary to see how long it lasts, because it is already known that now they do things so that they last less than 10 years.
Comments (Original): [ Esperaba algo mejor ] || ---------------- || Tenía un lavavajillas Fagor de los de antes, que me ha durado 27 años sin una sola reparación y lavaba genial. Era tosco y sin electrónica (programador mecánico, hacía bastante ruido, etc), pero lavaba genial y en 27 años ni un solo problema. Al final el pobre dijo basta y opté por este Bosch con ciertas reticencias porque el tema del wifi me parece una majadería que lo único que hace es meter electrónica sin sentido y encarecer las cosas. No lava bien, deja la vajilla bastante mojada, y a nada que haya alguna mancha un poco consistente, sale sucia la vajilla (lo cual no ocurría con el viejo Fagor). Eso sí, es bonito y muy silencioso, pero me he llevado una decepción. He probado con el programa eco (larguísimo) y el automático, y los resultados son similares. El tema de la app y el wifi, una tontería que desinstalé al minuto 0. En fin, no lo recomiendo, tengo otro de una marca supuestamente inferior (Beko) en otra casa y lava muchísimo mejor. Habrá que ver cuánto dura, porque ya se sabe que ahora hacen las cosas para que duren menos de 10 años.

Sentence (English): Advantages: The small kitchen is more convenient to use.
Comments (English): Advantages: The small kitchen is more convenient to use. I bought a silicone hose to connect the water from the water purifier for watering, so the convenience is good. You can use the dishwashing block of a small dishwasher for washing dishes. Because the water from the water purifier is used, there is no need to put dishwashing salt, and the dishwashing block can be solved in three in one. The dishes are clean. Be careful not to block the water arm with things placed on the upper layer. Disadvantages: 1. After washing the dishes, the lower bowls are basically dry, but there are still drops of water on the upper chopsticks and the upper and side walls of the dishwasher, and there is water under the filter; 2. Antibacterial storage cannot be opened separately The mode can only be turned on after washing the dishes, so if you accidentally touch the button, you have to wait for the next time to wash the dishes to turn on the antibacterial storage. Summary: In the case of using the water from the water purifier, the cost of each dishwashing is probably controlled within * yuan (dishwashing block 0.6-0.7+water 0.5+electricity 1.0), which is very cost-effective compared to my husband’s expensive labor costs of. Sentence (English): We love our Bosch 800 Series dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great Dishwasher - some minor annoyances ] || ---------------- || We love our Bosch 800 Series dishwasher. It's whisper quiet and does a fantastic job cleaning the dishes. I like the red light indicator - the dishwasher is so quiet, it's hard to tell when it's on and running. I have three annoyances with it, however. First, when the bottom rack is not fully loaded it can easily slide off the track. Second, the tines along the back of the bottom rack extend all the way to the edge, and so placing any large pan or cookie sheet is difficult. They need to end, one row in, allowing large pan placement. Finally, the silverware trays are garbage. For a premium dishwasher, Bosch should have done a better job with these. They do not stay stuck to the rack, and flop around everywhere. They are also too low, so that large kitchen spoons, spantulas, etc topple over (and then so does the basket because it isn't secured well.) Fix these things and the dishwasher will be perfect. Even with these small annoyances, we would still very much recommend the Bosch 800 series.

Sentence (English): We have had this unit for about 2 months now.
Comments (English): [ Cleans Great, but is far louder than advertised. ] || ---------------- || We have had this unit for about 2 months now. It does clean quite well, however it is FAR louder than the advertised 44 decibels. Full disclosure - I have reached out the the company asking for someone to come out and take a look, perhaps it is defective. But with my sound meter, I have measured at different points in the cycle. Many times it is above 52 decibels, which is completely unacceptable for a unit at this price point and one that advertises 44 max decibels. Another comment that we have found a little bit tiresome is the long cycle times. On the pro wash mode, with sanitize and high temp rinse modes on (we have 2 toddlers, so we run the dishwasher constantly and typically use hi temp and sani) the run time is over 3.5 hours. even without drying mode! This is tolerable, but everyone should be aware that the cycle run times are LONG. Hopefully Whirlpool/Kitchen Aid will resolve our units beyond acceptable volume issue, and I can update this review.
